+++
id = "23f492c8"
title = "Forward kinematics is a motor product"
created = 2026-11-17T18:19:22Z
updated = 2026-11-17T18:22:27Z
tags = ["ga/motion"]
aliases = ["forward kinematics"]
+++

A kinematic chain is a product of motors. For each joint $i$ with configuration
$q_i$, let $M_i (q_i)$ be that joint's motor — a rotor about an axis through a
point for a revolute joint, a translator for a prismatic one, the exponential of
a twist for a helical one — and let $F_i$ be the fixed transform from the
previous link frame to the joint. Then

```typst
M(q) = F_1 M_1 (q_1) F_2 M_2 (q_2) dots F_n M_n (q_n) F_(n + 1),
```

and the pose of any point or object attached to the tool is one
[[dc7fd3f4|The sandwich is an algebra automorphism]].

```ocaml
open Geom
let v3 x y z = Nx.create Nx.float32 [| 3 |] [| x; y; z |] in
let sc x = Nx.scalar Nx.float32 x in

let lengths = [| 0.65; 0.55; 0.45; 0.35; 0.30; 0.25 |] in
let q = [| 0.55; -0.75; 0.95; 0.35; -0.85; 0.65 |] in
let axis i = if i land 1 = 0 then v3 0. 0. 1. else v3 0. 1. 0. in
let joint i =
  Motor.mul (Motor.rotate ~axis:(axis i) ~angle:(sc q.(i)))
            (Motor.translate3 0. 0. lengths.(i))
in
let rec arm i =
  if i = Array.length lengths then Motor.one
  else Motor.mul (joint i) (arm (i + 1))
in
Nx.to_array (Cga.coords (Cga.apply_motor (arm 0) (Cga.point3 0. 0. 0.)))
(* [-0.9564, -0.2967, 2.156] *)
```

<figcaption style="text-align:center;font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.7;margin-top:0.4em">A planar arm built from motor products; the end-effector frame is one sandwich away from the pose motor.</figcaption>
</figure>

The order of the product matters and is easy to get wrong
([[5b1746c2|Motors compose like matrices]]). Every operation here is a product of eight-component
motors followed by a 32-component sandwich, both of which are small, batched and
differentiable
([[095f0641|The last axis is the blade axis]], [[863e305f|Traced algebra: no host branches]]). The chain is also a shortcut linear in each $q_i$ if
you differentiate it with `Rune.grad`, which is exactly what
[[f159d2a9|inverse kinematics]] exploits.
